Spanflug BUY is the platform for the efficient procurement of custom machined parts. By combining automation, intelligent algorithms, and a network of more than 8,000 machines, we find the optimal solution for each of your manufacturing tasks. Our end-to-end digital and automated processes, from quoting to order processing and delivery, reduce the workload for customers and suppliers by up to 90%, ensuring maximum efficiency. With automated processes, we accelerate the entire order processing and deliver your parts in as little as 5 working days. This shortens development cycles and gives you the flexibility to respond more quickly to market changes and position yourself for the future in global competition.

An innovative, AI-supported manufacturing algorithm understands your parts, ensuring maximum precision in costing, optimized order placement, and simplified work preparation. This reduces the complexity of the entire procurement process and minimizes economic risks.

As a partner in the CICAM project, Spanflug helped develop a calculation model for hybrid manufacturing: reliable cost prediction for parts built with WAAM and CNC.
How precise costing for hybrid manufacturing supports circular economy

The industry impact: only when the cost of a hybrid part is known in advance can manufacturers see whether this approach really is the most economical one, and choose the process that uses less material and takes less time. That is the promise of hybrid manufacturing, made tangible: parts produced at lower cost, with far less wasted raw material, making manufacturing more sustainable as a result.
WAAM as the basis for hybrid manufacturing

Most machined parts begin as a solid block of material. For many geometries, a significant share of it is removed during milling. Wire arc additive manufacturing (WAAM) follows the opposite principle: a part is built-up layer by layer, adding only the material required and close to the final contour.
These strengths make WAAM valuable across many industries, from aerospace and automotive to energy and general manufacturing. Typical use cases include:

Without a reliable prediction of what a given combination costs, it is not possible to identify the most efficient approach or assess the viability of the hybrid route. A central objective of CICAM was to establish the basis for a hybrid manufacturing cost prediction model. Spanflug took over responsibility for this task.

Spanflug has many years of experience in determining manufacturing times and costs for metal parts based on 3D models. Within CICAM, the technology company examined how this expertise, developed for conventional CNC machining, could be extended to additive as well as hybrid manufacturing, and what would be required to make the algorithms applicable to these new process chains.

Together, these contributions make hybrid manufacturing a real business decision, not just a technical option. Its costs, time, material use, and quality can now be assessed before a single part is made. Precise calculation is therefore not an academic exercise, but the basis for efficient and resource saving manufacturing.
